_note: Rotates one story per day. Read each passage in the NLT. Add more stories in the same shape.

stories.prayer: God, give me the strength to do the right thing when nobody's watching.
stories.q1: Joseph was a slave with nothing to lose by giving in. Why do you think he still said no?
stories.q2: He didn't argue with the temptation. He ran. What's one thing you should run from instead of negotiating with?
stories.q3: Joseph did the right thing and still ended up in prison. How do you keep going when doing right costs you?
stories.action: Name one temptation you usually negotiate with, and set up one barrier against it today.

stories.prayer: Lord, help me face today's giants with faith instead of fear.
stories.q1: David's confidence came from times God had already helped him. What has God already brought you through?
stories.q2: Saul's armor didn't fit David, so he used what he knew. What tools has God already put in your hands?
stories.q3: Everyone else saw how big Goliath was. David saw how big God was. What are you staring at too hard right now?
stories.action: Do the one task you've been avoiding because it feels too big. Start it before noon.

stories.prayer: God, make me consistent, the same man in private as in public.
stories.q1: Daniel's enemies couldn't find anything wrong with him except his faith. What would people find if they looked at your habits?
stories.q2: Daniel kept praying three times a day even when it became illegal. What daily habit with God would you protect at any cost?
stories.q3: Daniel was excellent at his job. How does doing your schoolwork well connect to your faith?
stories.action: Pick a set time to pray tomorrow and put it in your calendar.

stories.prayer: Father, thank you for running toward me when I come back.
stories.q1: The younger son 'came to his senses.' What usually makes you realize you've drifted?
stories.q2: The older brother never left, but he was still far from his father's heart. Where could you be doing the right things with the wrong heart?
stories.q3: What does the father running to his son tell you about how God sees your mistakes?
stories.action: Reach out to one person you've drifted from: a text, a call, or an apology.

stories.prayer: Lord, help me finish what I start, and keep building even when people mock it.
stories.q1: Sanballat mocked the builders. How do you handle people who doubt what you're building?
stories.q2: They worked with one hand and held a weapon in the other. What do you need to guard while you build?
stories.q3: The wall went up because everyone took their section. What's your section right now?
stories.action: Spend 25 minutes building something real (Jarvis, MATLAB, or your trade log) instead of scrolling.

stories.prayer: Jesus, teach me to lead by serving.
stories.q1: Jesus knew he had all authority, and he picked up a towel. What does that say about real strength?
stories.q2: Peter tried to refuse. Why is it sometimes harder to receive help than to give it?
stories.q3: Who around you needs a 'foot washing,' a humble act nobody would expect from you?
stories.action: Do one unasked-for chore or favor for someone at home today, and don't mention it.

stories.prayer: Lord, keep my eyes on you, not on the waves.
stories.q1: Peter was the only one who got out of the boat. What's a 'get out of the boat' step you've been holding back on?
stories.q2: He started sinking when he looked at the wind. What 'wind' pulls your focus off God?
stories.q3: Jesus caught him immediately. How does that change how you think about failing while trying?
stories.action: Take one step on something that scares you a little: ask a question in class, message your uncle, or similar.

stories.prayer: God, open my eyes to the people I usually walk past.
stories.q1: The priest and the Levite had reasons to keep walking. What reasons do you use to avoid getting involved?
stories.q2: The hero was someone the listeners looked down on. Who might you be underestimating?
stories.q3: The Samaritan paid with time and money. What would it cost you to really help someone this week?
stories.action: Notice one person who's struggling today and do something concrete for them.

stories.prayer: Lord, I'll trust you even when I feel like I don't have enough.
stories.q1: God cut Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300. Why would God make the odds worse on purpose?
stories.q2: Gideon needed reassurance more than once, and God gave it. How honest are you with God about your doubts?
stories.q3: Where in your life are you waiting to have 'enough' before you start?
stories.action: Start something today with what you have now, instead of waiting until you're ready.

stories.story: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness
stories.prayer: Jesus, help me answer temptation the way you did, with truth.
stories.q1: The devil came when Jesus was hungry and tired. When are you most vulnerable? Mornings, late nights?
stories.q2: Jesus answered every temptation with Scripture. What verse could you keep ready for your weak moments?
stories.q3: Each temptation offered a shortcut. What shortcut are you tempted by right now?
stories.action: Write one verse on a sticky note and put it where you usually grab your phone.
